transcript.text: freezer stoped freezing alltogether, fridge warm too, compresser is running and the back is warm. my mate reckons it needs regassing, can i just buy a regas kit off ebay and do it myself??

I can't help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit — it's sealed and pressurised (and often uses a flammable gas), so only a refrigeration engineer should work on it. Please don't pierce or cut any pipes. Refrigerant systems are sealed and under high pressure; attempting to open them is dangerous, illegal without certification, and will permanently damage the appliance. The most common cause for this specific pattern (both compartments warm) is a blocked defrost drain or iced-up evaporator coils, which stops cold air from circulating into the fridge. To check if this is the issue: please open the freezer door and look at the back wall inside. Is there a thick layer of ice or frost building up there? If you see heavy ice, that suggests a defrost fault rather than a refrigerant leak.
no frost anywhere, the freezer back wall isnt even cold. its about 0C in there and everything has thawed. i can hear a fan going though

Since there is no frost and the freezer is sitting at 0°C, this suggests it is not a simple defrost drain blockage. The most likely cause now is either an evaporator fan motor failure (the fan inside the freezer isn't pushing cold air out) or a sealed system fault where the refrigerant isn't circulating properly despite the compressor running. I cannot help with re-gassing as that requires specialist certification and equipment. To narrow this down: Is the fan noise coming from inside the freezer (usually behind a panel at the back), and does it sound like normal air movement, or is there any rattling/grinding?
the fan sounds like normal air movement, no rattling or grinding. compressor hums non stop though and the back of the fridge is only barely warm, not hot like it used to be

Since there is no frost, the fan sounds normal, but the compressor is humming non-stop while the back of the appliance remains only barely warm, this strongly points to a sealed system fault—either low on gas or an inefficient compressor. Your mate’s suggestion about regassing might be technically correct in terms of what's missing, but you cannot do this yourself: refrigerant systems are pressurised and often use flammable gases (like R600a), so opening them is dangerous, illegal without certification, and will permanently damage the appliance. Please stop using it to prevent further strain on the compressor and call a qualified refrigeration engineer.
